title: Have a mission
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What problem are you obsessed with fixing?

A mission-driven person naturally gravitates to solving a problem, I said. You talk to them and they are obsessed with: I want to fix this. I gave examples from the book's subject: colonize another planet so we have somewhere to live when the earth's resources run out, or stop burning fossil fuels by making electric cars.

If it doesn't have a big impact, the money didn't matter to him, I said. He could have gone to Wall Street with the offers he got, and he thought: they don't contribute anything to society, why would I do that?

I asked a student: what is your mission, as a person? The student said they did not have a clearly defined one. Another, asked what my mission is, said: to help people achieve success. I said: through education, to empower and help others, to teach business and coaching.

These are fundamental, I said. You should never have a question about what your mission is. It should be very transparent, repeatable, a promise. It should be the essence of what you do day to day, and you should never waver from it.
Having a mission puts you in the right place at the right time, I said, and creates intention. I added that it is part of developing your personal brand.

People call it meditating, visualizing or manifestation, I said. You don't have to use any of those names. What he is doing is being very clear on what he loves to study, and using his imagination to develop a plan to solve the problem.

groups.heading: A big problem, and a board of advisors

lines.text: The basis of a successful business, I said, is how big the problem is, how much you can solve it, and how valuable that is to people. The entrepreneur is obsessed with a problem.
I said the person in the book looked for mentors, and that is an important trait: you are open for advice. The first thing to do when you start a company is have a board of advisors.

There is nothing scarier for a venture capital fund, I said, than to fund a business with no good advisors. You are not going to give ten million dollars to one single guy who can wake up and decide to buy a plane, with nobody having any say.
Does your mission fix a problem?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your mission in one sentence.
Write whether it is transparent and repeatable enough that you could say it to a stranger.
Write who would be on your board of advisors.
Write one thing you do each day that is the essence of your mission.

check.q: How did I describe a mission-driven person?
choices: Someone who gravitates to solving a problem

check.q: What did I say a mission should be?
What did I say a venture fund is scared of?
choices: A business with no good board of advisors

recap: Know your mission and the problem it fixes. Keep advisors around you.
